findings.description: debtKind replaces every digit run with '#', so a re-gate flag that differs only by digits inside a name (e.g. "Nested package packages/app2 …" vs an open "packages/app1" entry) counts as already held and files no ledger entry, though decision 86 says a new kind is filed.

A re-gate refused only for an unaccepted flag (no failed stage) skips the new "Re-gate refused" branch and prints the generic advice to "steer the session", which a merged session doesn't have. It also never says the PR still vouches for the earlier pin.
Decision 86 says "an unaccepted flag refuses as a flagged merge does", but no test runs a re-gate that flags without `--accept-debt`; that branch in `regateMerged` and its CLI wording are untested.

`regateMerged(db, req, session, pullRequest, pullRequest.regate, ...)` passes `regate` twice, and `regate.prUrl` always equals `pullRequest.adoptedUrl` (planRegate enforces it); keep one source, e.g. `regate?: { head: string }` plus `adoptedUrl`.

`const regate = getSession(db, session)?.state === 'merged';` re-derives the core's dispatch rule in the CLI; have `MergeOutcome` carry a `regated` flag set by `regateMerged` so the CLI wording can't drift from the core.
`const regate = getSession(db, session)?.state === 'merged'` is a boolean that doesn't start with is/has/should/can (docs/conventions/general.md, Type safety); rename it `isRegate` or `shouldRegate`.
`held.has(debtKind(flag.description, session.id) as string)` casts away `undefined` and relies on `Set.has(undefined)` returning false; check `kind !== undefined && held.has(kind)` explicitly.
`COMMIT_SHA` is now exported from merge-gate.service.ts while dashboard.service.ts:337 still defines the identical regex privately; move it to merge-gate.constants.ts and share it with the dashboard.

Three re-gate refusal tests ("refuses a PR %s", "local branch is not at the PR head", "PR head reads back elsewhere") hand-write narrower subsets of the `expectRefusedUnwritten` checks instead of using the helper, leaving uneven nothing-was-written coverage.
Two tests repeat the same teardown (remove the `${SESSION_ID}-review` worktree, then `branch -D BRANCH`); fold it into a small helper or a `gateThenFix` option.
The `planRegate` JSDoc's last sentence, "The stages then measure that head, never anything the merge recorded.", describes `regateMerged`/`pinRegatedHead`, not `planRegate`'s contract; delete it.

The decision 84 amendment leaves one line far past the file's ~100-column wrap ('re-gate, and refuses an open PR whose head moved before it is merged. The fetch reads origin from the URL `pup init`'); re-wrap the paragraph.
